newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Feb fishmeal output falls to 49,800 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Feb fishmeal output falls to 49,800 tonnes.

text.p: Peru produced 49,800 tonnes of fishmeal in February, down from 117,800 tonnes in the same month last year, preliminary figures released by the Fisheries Ministry showed Tuesday.
Fishmeal production for the first two months of the year was 252,900 tonnes, down from 359,900 in the same period last year, the ministry said.

Exports of fishmeal for February reached 201,400 tonnes, up from 147,900 tonnes in the same month last year. Exports for the first two months of the year were 376,200 tonnes, up from 251,800 in the same period last year.
Officials have said the country's fishmeal production has fallen due to seasonal fishing bans and climatic factors while higher world prices have brought the overall hike in the value of exports.
Fishmeal, Peru's most important fishing product, accounted for 65 percent of the country's total processing of 76,700 tonnes of fish and other sea products in February.
Production of Peru's second most important fish product, raw fish oil, was 7,300 tonnes in February, down from 17,300 tonnes in the same month last year.
In February, the total catch of Peruvian fish and sea species was 304,900 tonnes, down from 600,400 tonnes in the same month last year.
Peru produced 1.885 million tonnes of fishmeal in 1996, up 5.4 percent from 1995. Last year's exports of fishmeal, however, fell 14 percent to 1.529 million tonnes.
